name: Banana
shortDescription: A fast-ripening fruit that changes quickly from green to spotted brown.
storageMethod: Keep bananas at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Once ripe, they can be moved to the refrigerator to slow further ripening, although the peel will darken.

shelfLife.roomTemperature: About 3–5 days once ripe (green bananas need a few extra days to ripen)
shelfLife.refrigerator: About 3–4 extra days once ripe (the peel darkens, but the fruit inside usually stays fine)
shelfLife.freezer: Peeled: about 3 months for best quality

storageTips: Separate bananas from the bunch to slow ripening slightly.
Keep them away from other fruit if you want to avoid speeding up ripening.
Peel and freeze overripe bananas in pieces for smoothies or baking.

freshnessStages.label: Underripe
freshnessStages.description: Green or very firm. Needs a few days at room temperature.

freshnessStages.label: Ripe
freshnessStages.description: Yellow and firm-soft. Sweet and easy to peel.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Brown spots and softer texture. Great for smoothies and baking.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Very dark, leaking or mushy. Look closely for mold or a sour smell.

freshnessSigns: Yellow peel with a few small spots
spoilageSigns: Visible mold on the peel or the flesh
Leaking liquid or very slimy texture

name: Apple
shortDescription: A crisp fruit that stores well when kept cool.
storageMethod: Apples keep their crispness longest in the refrigerator, ideally in the crisper drawer. At room temperature they soften faster.

shelfLife.refrigerator: About 4 weeks in the crisper drawer
shelfLife.freezer: Sliced or cooked: about 8 months for best quality (texture becomes soft)

storageTips: Store apples away from strongly scented foods.
Keep bruised apples separate so they do not affect the others.
Wash just before eating rather than before storing.

freshnessStages.label: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Firm, crisp and smooth-skinned.

freshnessStages.label: Softening
freshnessStages.description: Slightly soft or wrinkled. Better cooked than eaten raw.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Soft spots or bruises. Cut away small bruises or bake.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Mushy, leaking or moldy. Inspect carefully.

spoilageSigns: Large soft, brown or leaking areas

name: Strawberry
shortDescription: A delicate berry that softens and molds quickly.
storageMethod: Store unwashed strawberries in the refrigerator in a breathable container lined with paper towel. Wash only just before eating.

shelfLife.freezer: Washed, dried and hulled: about 10 months for best quality (texture becomes soft)

storageTips: Remove any soft or moldy berries right away so mold does not spread.
Do not wash until you are ready to eat them.
Freeze extra berries on a tray first, then move them to a bag.

freshnessStages.label: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Bright red, firm, with green leaves.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Slightly soft or darker. Good for smoothies or jam.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Mushy, leaking or with fuzzy patches. Check carefully for mold.

name: Tomato
shortDescription: Best ripened on the counter, then used within a few days.
storageMethod: Keep unripe tomatoes at room temperature out of direct sun until they ripen. Ripe tomatoes can go in the refrigerator if you cannot use them in time; bring them to room temperature before eating for better flavour.
shelfLifePreview: Room temp: about 2–3 days once ripe

shelfLife.roomTemperature: Ripe: about 2–3 days. Unripe: about 3–5 days to ripen first
shelfLife.refrigerator: About 5 days once ripe (flavour and texture may dull)
shelfLife.freezer: Best for cooking: about 2 months (texture becomes soft)

storageTips: Store stem-side down to reduce bruising.
Do not stack tomatoes; they bruise easily.
Freeze soft tomatoes and use them in sauces or soups.

freshnessStages.label: Ripening
freshnessStages.description: Firm and still pale. Leave at room temperature.

freshnessStages.label: Ripe
freshnessStages.description: Deep colour, slight give and a tomato smell.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Soft and wrinkly skin. Good for sauces and soups.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Leaking, collapsing or moldy. Inspect carefully.

name: Potato
shortDescription: A hardy vegetable that lasts weeks in a cool, dark place.
storageMethod: Store potatoes in a cool, dark, well-ventilated place. Avoid sunlight, which can turn them green. Do not keep them next to onions.

shelfLife.pantry: About 3–4 weeks in a cool, dark, ventilated place
shelfLife.freezer: Only after cooking or blanching: about 3 months (raw potatoes freeze poorly)

storageTips: Keep potatoes in a paper bag or basket, not sealed plastic.
Remove any spoiled potato so the others stay in good condition.
Avoid washing until you are ready to cook.

freshnessStages.label: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Firm, smooth skin with no sprouts.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Small sprouts or slight softening. Use soon and remove sprouts.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Green patches, heavy sprouting, shriveling or softness. When in doubt, avoid.

name: Spinach
shortDescription: Tender leafy greens that wilt quickly if stored damp.
storageMethod: Keep spinach in the refrigerator in a container lined with paper towel to absorb moisture. Wash just before using.

shelfLife.refrigerator: About 5 days (bagged spinach: follow the product label)
shelfLife.freezer: Blanched: about 10 months for best quality (texture becomes soft)

storageTips: Moisture speeds up spoilage, so keep leaves dry.
Remove any slimy leaves as soon as you see them.
Wilted but otherwise fresh spinach is best cooked.

freshnessStages.label: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Crisp, bright green leaves.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Slightly wilted. Best cooked in soup or stir-fries.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Slimy, yellowing or smelly. Avoid if in doubt.

name: Milk
shortDescription: A cold-chain dairy staple that should be kept refrigerated.
storageMethod: Store milk in the main body of the refrigerator (not the door) and keep the container closed. Do not leave it out for long periods.

shelfLife.refrigerator: About 5–7 days after opening; unopened milk: use by the label date
shelfLife.freezer: About 3 months (leave space in the container; texture may separate)

storageTips: Return milk to the refrigerator right after pouring.
Never pour used milk back into the container.
Check the product label and storage instructions on the pack.

freshnessStages.label: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Cold, sealed or recently opened, with a mild smell.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Nearing the label date or opened for several days.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Sour smell, lumps or unusual look. Do not consume if in doubt.

name: Yogurt
shortDescription: A cultured dairy food that keeps well when cold.
storageMethod: Keep yogurt tightly covered in the refrigerator. Use a clean spoon each time to avoid introducing contamination.

shelfLife.refrigerator: About 5–7 days after opening; unopened: use by the label date
shelfLife.freezer: About 2 months (texture becomes grainy or watery)

storageTips: Keep the lid on tightly after each use.
A little watery liquid on top can be normal; stir it in and check smell and appearance.
Do not leave yogurt out of the refrigerator for long periods.

freshnessStages.label: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Smooth, creamy and pleasantly tangy.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Nearing the label date or opened for several days.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Mold, strong sour smell or unusual look. Avoid if in doubt.

name: Cheese
shortDescription: Shelf life depends a lot on type, from soft cheeses to hard blocks.
storageMethod: Wrap cheese in wax paper or parchment, then place it in a loose container in the refrigerator. Do not wrap it too tightly in plastic for long periods.

shelfLife.refrigerator: Hard cheese: about 3–4 weeks after opening. Soft cheese: about 1–2 weeks after opening
shelfLife.freezer: About 2 months for best quality (texture becomes crumbly)

storageTips: Wrap each type of cheese separately.
Use clean utensils to cut cheese.
For soft cheese with mold, follow food-safety guidance or avoid it.

freshnessStages.label: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Normal colour, smell and texture for its type.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Dry edges, sweating or opened for a while.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Mold, slime or sharp off smell. Avoid soft cheese with mold; check guidance for hard cheese.

spoilageSigns: Visible mold, especially on soft cheese

name: Bread
shortDescription: Goes stale within days, but the freezer extends its life.
storageMethod: Keep bread in a breadbox or sealed bag at room temperature. Freeze slices if you will not finish the loaf within a few days.

shelfLife.roomTemperature: About 4–5 days for packaged sliced bread; bakery loaves are best within 2–3 days

storageTips: The refrigerator can dry bread out faster, so room temperature or freezer is usually better.
Slice before freezing so you can take out only what you need.
Stale bread is a quality issue, not necessarily a safety issue, and is good for toast or breadcrumbs.

freshnessStages.label: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Soft with a pleasant smell.

freshnessStages.label: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Getting dry or stale. Good for toast, croutons or breadcrumbs.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Any visible mold or a musty smell. Avoid the whole loaf.

spoilageSigns: Green, white or black mold spots

name: Rice
shortDescription: Dry rice keeps for a long time; cooked rice needs quick, careful storage.
storageMethod: Keep dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry pantry. For cooked rice, cool it quickly, store it in the refrigerator, and reheat until steaming hot.
shelfLifePreview: Dry: about 1 year · Cooked: 3–4 days in fridge

shelfLife.pantry: Dry white rice: about 1 year for best quality. Brown rice: about 6 months
shelfLife.refrigerator: Cooked rice: about 3–4 days in a sealed container
shelfLife.freezer: Cooked rice: about 1 month for best quality

storageTips: Do not leave cooked rice at room temperature for long; refrigerate it within about 1–2 hours.
Store dry rice away from moisture and pests.
Reheat cooked rice until steaming hot and do it only once.

freshnessStages.label: Dry: Stable
freshnessStages.description: Uncooked rice kept dry and sealed stays good for a long time.

freshnessStages.label: Cooked: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Just cooked, cooled quickly and stored in the refrigerator.

freshnessStages.label: Cooked: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Second or third day in the refrigerator. Use in fried rice.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Slimy, hard or smelly rice. Avoid if in doubt.

freshnessSigns: Dry rice: no moisture or clumping
Cooked rice: fluffy and neutral smell
spoilageSigns: Damp clumps, mold or insects in dry rice

name: Pasta
shortDescription: Dry pasta is a long-lasting pantry staple; cooked pasta is short-lived.
storageMethod: Keep dry pasta in a sealed container in a cool, dry pantry. Refrigerate cooked pasta in an airtight container within about 2 hours.
shelfLifePreview: Dry: about 2 years · Cooked: 3–4 days in fridge

shelfLife.pantry: Dry pasta: about 2 years for best quality
shelfLife.refrigerator: Cooked pasta: about 3–4 days in a sealed container
shelfLife.freezer: Cooked pasta: about 2 months for best quality

storageTips: Store dry pasta away from moisture and pests.
Toss cooked pasta with a little oil before storing to prevent sticking.
Reheat cooked pasta until steaming hot.

freshnessStages.label: Dry: Stable
freshnessStages.description: Uncooked pasta stays good for a long time when kept dry.

freshnessStages.label: Cooked: Fresh
freshnessStages.description: Freshly cooked or newly refrigerated.

freshnessStages.label: Cooked: Use Soon
freshnessStages.description: Several days in the refrigerator. Use in a bake or stir-fry.

freshnessStages.label: Check Quality
freshnessStages.description: Slimy texture, smell or mold. Avoid if in doubt.

freshnessSigns: Cooked pasta: firm and neutral smell
spoilageSigns: Moisture, mold or insects in dry pasta
